subject: docs/coop/artifacts/deferral.DR-106-109-113.preview.v2.json
reviewClass: independent, refute not confirm; D-001/D-002 explicit-deferral candidate covering three rows
summary: The named attack here is inventing a typed purge result, and this candidate is built around refusing exactly that — its whyWholly reproduces D-002's own reasoning, including that splitting a purge half of DR-113 would design the typed purge result DR-007 forbids inventing, and that the slice's local purge/doctor routes through DR-124/DR-114/DR-G12/DR-107 instead. All three owner strings match file 08 character-for-character, all three rows lead OPEN and inherit-blocked as D-001 classifies them, and the severability clause stops one shared draft from becoming one indivisible recording.
whatIVerified: Subject digest at start and end: 194b01fc6bd9201ebdeee71b83846cff09417d7521464bd81a0fbe2aabf7502c, three measurements at the start and two at the close, equal to the dispatched value, -r--r--r-- throughout. The prompt held at 6a46241c… across start and end.

The attack 'invents typed purge result' fails, and the refusal is D-002's own rather than the drafter's invention. D-002 reads: 'correcting the previous draft's unlawful row splits (turn-1 MF-03) — DR-106, DR-109 and DR-113 are deferred WHOLLY: their acceptance-evidence cells all begin with applied DR-002..008 successors, and DR-113's "purge half" would have designed the typed purge result DR-007 expressly forbids inventing. The slice's local purge/doctor needs route through DR-124/DR-114/DR-G12/DR-107 instead.' The artifact's whyWholly reproduces that reasoning and its decision reproduces the routing, naming DR-124 / DR-114 / DR-G12 / DR-107 in the same order. whatThisDoesNotDo closes with an explicit 'Does not invent a typed purge result.'

The wholly-deferred claim is D-002's and is quoted accurately in both places D-002 states it — the explicit-deferrals paragraph, 'DR-106, DR-109, DR-113, each deferred WHOLLY (T2-01: the previous "halves" wording here contradicted the entry's own MF-03 withdrawal and is struck)', and the State paragraph. The artifact's commission cites MF-03 and T2-01 by name, and both citations are real.

All three owner assignments match the register character-for-character, which I checked rather than accepted: file 08 gives DR-106 'Product + evidence + release', DR-109 'Evidence + storage architecture' and DR-113 'Evidence + product', identical to the artifact's ownerWhoMustRecord map. The map is per-row rather than a single blanket owner, which is what makes three separate recordings possible.

The severability clause does real work and is not boilerplate. It states that the three rows share one fact but that adopting or overturning one recording does not adopt or overturn the others, and that a later D-000 entry must name which row it records. Without it a single shared draft could be recorded once and read as disposing of three rows at three different owners; with it, the condition-2 effect is confined to 'the named row only'.

The three rows' standing in the register is consistent with a wholly-deferred inherit-blocked treatment: all three lead OPEN and their status cells begin 'OPEN / inherits hard…', and D-001's condition-2 classification places them in the 'Inherit-blocked' set rather than among the route-C product decisions or the rule-governed authoring rows. So the artifact's account of why they cannot be split — their acceptance evidence begins with applied DR-002..008 successors — matches how the register already classifies them.

The attack 'pulls deferred surface into preview' fails, and each of the three admissions traces to something D-002 includes. 'Non-authoritative preview analyze/doctor output' is the honest complement of authoritative closure being OUT; 'Rebuildable cache/index and Operational metadata (DR-124 classes D-002 includes)' matches D-002's inclusion of DR-124 classes; and 'Local doctor/purge honesty that does not invent a typed sealed-Run purge result' carries the prohibition inside the admission itself, which is the right construction for the one surface where the line is easiest to cross.

The exclusion list holds the authoritative surfaces outside — signed offline authoritative analysis closure, the host-owned storage-mechanics interface for authoritative commit, and replay/verification/inspection/purge/degradation of sealed evidence — and adds DR-G06 and DR-G11 as gates that guard authoritative closure and storage and are not slice-1-required. That last item matches D-002's own 'G06/G11: NOT slice-1-required'.

The attack 'silent SATISFIED' fails: status CANDIDATE-NOT-RECORDED, binds NOTHING, DO-NOT-SEAL, and the SATISFIED occurrences are refusals — 'Does not mark DR-106, DR-109, or DR-113 SATISFIED' and 'Does not SATISFY any of the three'. whatThisDoesNotDo also refuses to select Route B for DR-002..008, which is the adjacent overreach available to a row whose evidence inherits from those successors.

The attacks 'coordinator pretending to be owner', 'authorizing implementation', 'amending D-002' and 'file 08 edited' fail: the owner map is per-row and the effect is conditional on owner recording throughout, reversibility is 'Total before owner recording', and whatThisDoesNotDo refuses implementation and file-08 edits. file 08 measures 45dc4611… unmodified in my working tree.

The attack 'stale recordedInputs' fails. COORD 4ec06988… and file 08 45dc4611… both equal live bytes at the start and again at the close, and the remeasuredAfter marker f7ce35ff… resolves to 'D-093: record committed host-effect-authorization.v8 candidate'.
The frozen v1 predecessor is unedited: deferral.DR-106-109-113.preview.v1.json hashes 0c0cd74091d9b711db90fdf75e2e456a015fcacc6be529b96506156aa9730f1d, matching predecessorSha256.
I wrote one file, the verdict named for me, and edited and committed nothing.

acceptNote: ACCEPT at zero blockers and zero advisories. The interesting property of this candidate is that it is a single draft covering three rows with three different owners, which is the shape most likely to produce an accidental collective recording — and the severability clause forecloses that in terms, requiring a later entry to name which row it records. On the substance it does not merely avoid inventing a typed purge result; it explains, in D-002's own reasoning, why the split that would have required inventing one was withdrawn, and it carries the prohibition inside the very admission where the temptation lives.
